sections.h2: Which sale route is fastest for a Troy homeowner?
sections.html:
Troy sellers can price a listing to draw several bids, find their own buyer, or take a cash purchase with no repair demands. Troy's median home value tops Sterling Heights, Taylor and Walker in the Census figures, so weeks of preparation can pay off, while a cash deal suits an owner with no time to spare.

Owners' median home value is $420,300 and median household income is $120,045 for 2020 through 2024. At that level, a buyer's inspection report carries weight. Major repairs, an estate to settle or a job transfer can push a seller toward a single offer from someone who absorbs the work.

  • Agent listing: best for a house in good order when inspections and lender timelines are acceptable.
  • Private sale: workable if you can draft a contract and a deed the county will record.
  • Cash offer: right when speed, privacy or condition matter more than top dollar.

sections.h2: Where is Troy, and how did the city develop?
sections.html:
Oakland County's Troy holds 33.45 square miles of land and an estimated 88,733 residents as of mid-2025, with Sterling Heights on its eastern edge.

Buyers bought the first recorded land in 1819, and Troy Corners grew where a settler purchased 160 acres in what is now north-central Troy. A township formed in 1827, and pieces of it later went to Birmingham, Clawson and Royal Oak. The rest became the city in 1955, partly to keep neighbors from taking more territory. The city is named for Troy, New York, because many early settlers came from New York. Government is council-manager, with a mayor and six council members who appoint a city manager to run daily operations. Growth was sharp: 19,402 people in 1960, 39,419 in 1970, and 87,294 at the 2020 Census.

In the 48098 ZIP code the January average low is 22 degrees Fahrenheit and yearly precipitation totals near 32 inches, so inspectors look closely at roofs and gutters.

sections.html:

sections.h2: How large is Troy's commercial base?
sections.html:
The city's commerce is bigger than its population suggests. Retail sales reached $4.17 billion in 2022 (Census), about $47,709 per resident and far above Sterling Heights, Taylor or Walker. Health care and social assistance took in $2.28 billion, and lodging and restaurants $536 million.

Also per Census, 65.8% of residents over 16 are in the labor force, and 2,577 veterans live here. A seller benefits from that base of nearby jobs.

City Hall at 500 W. Big Beaver Road houses the Assessor, the Clerk and the Treasurer, so records requests and tax receipts can usually be handled in one trip. Dog licenses come through Oakland County Animal Control, and Troy does not impose a general business license.

sections.h2: Which employers, malls and schools shape Troy demand?
sections.html:
Big Beaver Road anchors the business district. Automotive and financial offices line it, the Somerset Collection mall (180 stores and a skywalk) and the Oakland Mall draw shoppers, and the Top of Troy houses a PNC office. Walsh College and several branch campuses operate in town, and the Troy Historic Village preserves ten buildings from the city's past.

Seven districts divide Troy. The home district for most addresses is Troy School District, with twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, Troy High and Athens High, plus the International Academy's eastern campus. Elementary buildings inside the city also belong to Avondale, Birmingham and Warren Consolidated, while Bloomfield Hills, Royal Oak and Lamphere cover small areas.

Neighbors may attend different districts, so state the district in your listing and double-check addresses near a boundary.

sections.h2: How do assessments and tax bills affect a Troy seller?
sections.html:
Under the state constitution, Troy's assessor sets values at half of market value, and the same office runs Principal Residence Exemption and Property Transfer Affidavit programs. Its 2026 projection puts the combined State Equalized Value above $10 billion.

  • Summer bill: goes out July 1 and is clear of penalty through September 1. A 4% charge follows, with half a percent monthly starting October 1.
  • Winter bill: goes out December 1 and is clear through February 14, followed by 3%.
  • On March 1, open current-year balances shift to the Oakland County Treasurer at 248.858.0611, option 7.

Troy collects for seven school districts plus the county, Oakland Schools, Macomb Intermediate and several county authorities. School levies change with the district and with principal-residence status, so look-alike houses can get different bills. Homeowners who are 62 or older, disabled or veterans, with income of $40,000 or below, may defer to April 30 by applying through September 15.

Under Michigan law the buyer's taxable value uncaps the year after a transfer. Prorations are set by contract, and the Treasurer's Office at 248.524.3333 can describe the amount due on a given date.

sections.h2: What does selling in Oakland County cost at the Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Transfer tax is the seller's, due within 15 days of delivery of the deed (MCL 207.523). The state share is $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525). MCL 207.504 sets the county share at 55 cents per $500 where a county has fewer than 2,000,000 residents, so confirm the Oakland County figure with the register before closing.

The Register of Deeds answers at 248-858-0597 or deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov, on weekdays, with counter hours starting at 8:30 in the morning. It files deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records, and its Super Index lets you pull recorded documents back to January 1, 1964.

Gifts to children and grandchildren, deeds in foreclosure and court orders with no stated price are exempt under MCL 207.526, and the deed must name the exemption on its face.

sections.h2: What Troy property rules should be settled before showings?
sections.html:
Code Enforcement publishes the complaints it handles most often. A quick walk around the lot can head off a notice during your listing.

  • Lawn grass and weeds stay under 8 inches between May 1 and October 31, including the strip to the road.
  • Snow over 2 inches and ice come off public sidewalks within 24 hours after a storm.
  • Vehicles kept on private land must carry current plates and run, and RVs cannot sit on the street.
  • Temporary signs are allowed on private property, while signs in the public right-of-way are removed.
  • Bins go to the curb after 5 p.m. the day before pickup, and branches near sidewalks need trimming to 8 feet.

Keep open house and yard signs on your own lot. Two more rules matter to some sellers: one commercial pickup or cargo van may sit on private property in a one-family district, and home businesses are allowed in one- and two-family districts under conditions, so a buyer planning to work from the house should call Code Enforcement first.

faqs.q: What is a typical Troy home worth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes is $420,300. Individual houses vary with age, lot and district.

faqs.q: When do Troy tax bills come due?
faqs.a: Summer bills are payable until September 1 and winter bills until February 14. Anything unpaid on March 1 goes to Oakland County.

faqs.q: Do Troy taxes reset after I sell?
faqs.a: For the buyer, yes. Taxable value uncaps in the calendar year after a transfer of ownership.

faqs.q: Which school district is a Troy house in?
faqs.a: Most houses are in Troy School District, but Avondale, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Lamphere, Royal Oak and Warren Consolidated also cover parts of the city.

faqs.q: Where is a Troy deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Oakland County Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597. Transfer tax is collected unless the deed cites an exemption.
